provenance.pins: two-terminal Schottky, DO-214AC/SOD outline: pin 1 = cathode-band end, pin 2 = opposite. Polarity from the package drawing, not inferred from function

designVerdict: SELECTED as D14 - lifts the HUSB238A VBUS pin at vSafe5V, where the emitter follower falls short.
notes: Anode on the 5 V rail, cathode on the HUSB238A VBUS pin. At a 4.75 V bus the rail is 4.56 V (the TPS54360B's own dropout, worked from Eq. 1 with the real inductor DCR) and this part drops 0.37 V max at 1 mA (p.2), holding the pin at 4.19 V against a 3.15 V minimum - where the follower alone gives 3.05-3.75 V and fails.

It conducts only at low bus voltage. Once the bus rises the follower takes the pin to ~26.3 V and this diode is reverse-biased by 21.3 V, inside its 40 V rating - including during a 58.1 V TVS clamp, because the follower's Zener holds the pin at 26.3 V regardless of the collector.
Chosen for low Vf at small current rather than for current capability: the load is 800 uA max. A 1N5819-class power Schottky would drop more at this current, which is the opposite of what is wanted.
